questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to check over your shoulder if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Other drivers will always respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. A tire that looks okay might actually be under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: What does a rectangular sign usually show?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black lettering show traffic rules like speed limits. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have very small blind spots that don't cause problems.
Have blind spots that you must check by turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you must check by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which item will NOT help reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for best protection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is legal?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit until you finish passing.
You can ignore "No passing zone" markings if you started in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must finish passing within the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must finish passing within the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always pass within posted speed limits. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When switching lanes, what should you do about blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so other vehicles can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: An approved helmet should:

options.text: Allow you to see far to the sides as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see to the sides as needed for safe riding. All approved helmets have labels with the maker's name, instructions, and safety standard information.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes less than eyeglasses do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield protects your whole face. Eyeglasses are not a good substitute for either goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Use it only on cloudy days.
Use it if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use it.
questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from the alcohol may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your body even if you drink only one drink per hour. Your abilities and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: Which type of material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: Before every ride, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will most likely know you are there.
You are preventing other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This way, you will be visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Check your tires for all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: A way to reduce the risk of a crash is to:

options.text: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
Ride in positions that make it hard to be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by staying visible to others. Signal your intentions with your signals, brake light, and lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and constantly scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes smoothly and gradually for the shortest, safest stops. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
Let air out of the tires.
Not tell passengers about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. You need more space between your bike and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, what should you do with them?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in.
questions.explanation: Tuck your laces in securely so they don't catch on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing where to ride in your lane?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position than another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose your position in the lane so other drivers can see you. Also make sure you have enough space between your bike and other vehicles.

questions.question: If your motorcycle takes longer to stop than normal, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your bike and the vehicle ahead. This gives you more time to stop.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.
